evals.query: My agent is spending most of its context just ferrying API responses back and forth — one Cloudflare call alone blew past a million tokens. How do agents avoid paying for raw API payloads?
evals.prompt: My agent is spending most of its context just ferrying API responses back and forth — one Cloudflare call alone blew past a million tokens. How do agents avoid paying for raw API payloads?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Code-Over-API (references/code-over-api-pattern-report.md): the agent writes code that runs against the API in a sandboxed environment and returns only the summary, rather than pulling payloads through the context window. Should carry the documented scale (75-2,000x, with the Cloudflare case cited at 99.95%) and the path.
assertions: grounds the recommendation in the report's own figures rather than an invented number
does not tell the user to truncate raw API responses as a substitute

evals.query: Untrusted web content is sitting in my agent's context for the whole session and I am worried about a later instruction in it being obeyed. What is the pattern for this?
evals.prompt: Untrusted web content is sitting in my agent's context for the whole session and I am worried about a later instruction in it being obeyed. What is the pattern for this?
evals.expected_output: Recommends the Context-Minimization Pattern (references/context-minimization-pattern-report.md): treat context as a staged pipeline — ingest untrusted text, transform it, then discard it — which removes the delayed prompt-injection exposure and cuts token use (10-100x as documented), with the path and status.
assertions: connects minimisation to the delayed prompt-injection class specifically
does not propose leaving untrusted content resident and merely warning about it

evals.query: My agent keeps reasoning its way past the safety rules I put in its system prompt. What is the structural fix?
evals.prompt: My agent keeps reasoning its way past the safety rules I put in its system prompt. What is the structural fix?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Hook-Based Safety Guard Rails (references/hook-based-safety-guard-rails-report.md): run the safety check outside the agent's reasoning loop at PreToolUse/PostToolUse, so the agent cannot rationalise past it, since a constraint inside the prompt is just more text the model can argue with. Cites the path and status.
assertions: places enforcement outside the reasoning loop rather than in the prompt
does not recommend strengthening the system-prompt wording as the primary fix

evals.query: I am shipping an agent that can make outbound calls and I need to be sure it cannot be talked into posting secrets somewhere. What do I put in front of it?
evals.prompt: I am shipping an agent that can make outbound calls and I need to be sure it cannot be talked into posting secrets somewhere. What do I put in front of it?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Egress Lockdown (No-Exfiltration Channel) (references/egress-lockdown-no-exfiltration-channel-report.md) — an egress control with domain-level outbound restrictions so no exfiltration channel exists to be used — and pairs it with the hook-based guard rails and context minimisation for defence in depth, with paths and statuses.
assertions: removes the channel at the network layer rather than relying on the model's judgement
pairs the control with the wider security stack rather than presenting it as sufficient alone

evals.query: An autonomous agent on our team has no notion of spend and keeps picking the most expensive model. How do I make cost a hard constraint instead of a suggestion?
evals.prompt: An autonomous agent on our team has no notion of spend and keeps picking the most expensive model. How do I make cost a hard constraint instead of a suggestion?
evals.expected_output: Recommends Budget-Aware Model Routing with Hard Cost Caps (references/budget-aware-model-routing-with-hard-cost-caps-report.md): an explicit budget contract with caps that bind, and SLA-aware routing across tiers (the report covers FrugalGST, RouteLLM and xRouter) selecting the cheapest model that still meets the quality bar. Cites the path and status.
assertions: makes the cap a binding constraint rather than a prompt-level preference
does not answer by simply hard-coding a cheaper model

evals.query: I am new to this codebase's agent work and want the lay of the land — every agent pattern you have, how they group, and which ones are meant to be used together.
evals.prompt: I am new to this codebase's agent work and want the lay of the land — every agent pattern you have, how they group, and which ones are meant to be used together.
evals.expected_output: Starts from the master taxonomy (references/01-pattern-taxonomy.md) to lay out the full pattern space, cross-category relationships and the composition guide, before recommending any individual report.

evals.prompt: Which agentic pattern should I reach for when I want a quick read on a couple of hundred patterns rather than a deep dive on one? I just want to browse the catalogue.
